subject: Performance SLO follow-up: Nova Retail - latency & cost levers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novaretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up: Nova Retail - latency & cost levers

Hi Samir / Priya -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before running benchmarks: 

Summary of requirements you called out
- P95 end-to-end latency SLO: 200ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) for the customer-facing chat widget
- Streaming required (time-to-first-token matters)
- Expected steady-state concurrency: ~100 concurrent chat sessions, with burst capacity to 500 for promotional spikes
- Typical prompt length: 40-120 tokens. Long-running background jobs to index docs are separate and lower priority.

Primary questions we need to validate in the benchmark
- Confirm time-to-first-token (streaming) at 100c and at burst (500c)
- Verify cold-start behavior and tail latencies during sudden scale-up
- Understand throughput (tokens/sec) requirements to size GPU pools and batching windows

Cost / performance levers we recommend to hit the SLO
1) Continuous batching: use a short batching window (we typically start at 10-25ms for low-latency chat) to increase token throughput without adding perceptible latency. This reduces per-token cost substantially at scale.
2) Prefix / KV caching: cache common system prompts and user prefixes (TTL configurable). For chat flows with repeated contexts, this can eliminate repeated compute for the prefix and cut token cost.
3) Quantization profiles & model variants: recommend evaluating an int8 quantized variant for the primary workload (small latency increase, large cost reduction). Keep a higher-precision variant for the most latency-sensitive / high-accuracy flows.
4) Dynamic routing & fallbacks: route non-critical reads to cheaper model variants or batch-only nodes; keep dedicated low-latency pool for interactive sessions.
5) Autoscale + reserved capacity: configure a baseline reserved pool sized for steady-state (100c) and autoscaling for bursts.

Initial config we suggest for the benchmark
- Batch window: 20ms
- KV cache TTL: 10 minutes (tunable)
- Model variants: rwd-base-v2-int8 (primary), rwd-base-v2-fp16 (fallback for high-accuracy)
- Target arrival pattern: steady 100c (1s think time) + 1:10 spike to 500c for 2 minutes

Attachments: redwood-performance-options.pdf (overview of levers), nova-cost-modeling.xlsx (back-of-envelope cost scenarios)

Next steps
- You to share a sample production traffic trace (anonymized) or representative qps pattern - we can replay for realistic batching and cache warm-up
- We run an initial 2-hour benchmark and share P95/Tail/first-token numbers + cost sensitivity tables
- Follow-up call to review results and agree on a pilot configuration

Can we schedule the benchmark run for Wed (Mar 17) or Thu (Mar 18)? Also please share procurement contact so we can surface a pilot/PO if the numbers look good.

Thanks -
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa - great writeup and exactly what we need. A couple quick clarifications before we hand over traffic: 

1) When you say 200ms P95 for short prompts, is that measured as time-to-first-token (streaming) or time-to-full-completion? For chat UX the first-token matters more, but we need both numbers.
2) How does caching work across sessions? Our chat context often changes per user - will prefix caching still help?
3) Cold starts: if we scale from 100 -> 500 quickly, do we expect a significant tail spike? Any mitigations we should plan for?

Also - can you provide a ballpark cost for ~1M tokens/day using the int8 variant vs fp16? Enough to get procurement started. I'll loop in our procurement lead once we have a rough number.

Priya, let me know if Wed or Thu works for you for a benchmark window.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@novaretail.com>, Priya Singh <priya@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up: Nova Retail - latency & cost levers

Samir - good questions, answers inline and a few concrete numbers so procurement can start a review.

1) 200ms SLO: we interpreted your UX ask as P95 time-to-first-token (streaming). For short prompts that typically aligns with perceived latency. We'll report both metrics in the benchmark: time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token (completion). Expect time-to-first-token ~180-220ms and completion times varying by prompt length.

2) Prefix caching: two levels - static system prompts (very high hit rate) + per-user prefix cache. Even with per-user variance, common system tokens and repeated instructions still benefit. For highly unique per-user history the benefit is smaller but KV caching still reduces initial KV recompute costs for tokens that repeat across users (e.g., structured system tokens, frequently used templates).

3) Cold starts and scaling: cold-start tail is typically driven by model load and kernel warm-up. Mitigations: keep a small warm pool (hot replicas) and warm additional nodes proactively during anticipated promos. On our platform we can provision warm-up capacity for the expected spike window to avoid large tail latency. We'll include a cold-start test in the benchmark (rapid ramp) and show tail behavior.

Ballpark costs (very rough back-of-envelope for 1M tokens/day)
- rwd-base-v2-fp16 (high-accuracy): ~$950/day
- rwd-base-v2-int8 (quantized): ~$420/day
Assumptions: avg prompt+response 120 tokens, steady distribution, includes model infer compute only (excludes storage/ingest/observability addons). We'll provide a detailed cost sensitivity sheet after the benchmark run.

Benchmark agenda we propose
- 15m: kickoff & signals to monitor
- 60m: steady-state runs at 100c
- 20m: ramp tests to 500c (short bursts)
- 25m: cold-start / warmup tests

I've attached the same cost workbook and our options deck. Rishi / Dev will take point on the run; they may reach out with a short list of config params we should toggle.

If Wed (Mar 17) 10:00am PT works we can lock it - otherwise Thu morning also ok.

Thanks -
Marissa
